title: fastpath: gating + safe-mode + precision-toggle + KV scheduler fallback
description: This changeset introduces a safer fast-path gating strategy and improved fallback handling to reduce correctness/perf tradeoffs observed under mixed-precision and high-concurrency workloads. Motivation: we observed intermittent correctness rollbacks and fallback thrash when the fast-path kernels failed under FP16/INT8 transitions or transient allocator pressure during continuous batching. This PR implements three coordinated changes: 1) fast-path gating policy that verifies kernel and tensor precision compatibility before dispatch and falls back deterministically to the slow path when invariants are not met, 2) a runtime precision-toggle that allows an in-flight request to switch precision safely while keeping the KV cache coherent (includes cache versioning and a lightweight rekey when precision changes), and 3) scheduling updates to the continuous batcher so it prefers stable fast-path-compatible batches and preempts batches that would cause frequent fallbacks. The implementation includes unit and integration tests, a small perf harness, and regression checks to prevent future behavior regressions. Benchmarks: mixed CPU/GPU inference workloads show ~12% reduction in p99 latency and ~6% throughput improvement in steady-state for long-context streaming workloads with KV cache hits, and reduced fallback rate from ~3.8% to ~0.2%. See commits and CI for details.

notes: This PR touches low-level kernels and scheduling. Ops: rollout behind runtime flag fastpath.safe_mode=false by default; recommend enabling in canary for 48h and monitor fastpath.fallback_rate and scheduler.preempt_events.
